chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come in my Ummah when their inner selves will become impure and their outer appearances will become attractive, out of greed for the world, not seeking what is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Their affairs will be for show (riya'), fear will not accompany them, Allah will encompass them with punishment, so they will supplicate to Him with the supplication of a drowning man, and their supplication will not be answered.'
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a hypocritical era in the Muslim Ummah according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this eschatological sign of spiritual decay, where the disconnect between inner sincerity (ikhlas) and outer piety leads to a state of divine neglect. The metaphor of the 'drowning man's supplication' underscores the futility of ritual prayer devoid of presence of heart, a key concept in Shia ethical theology. This narration serves as a warning against the corruption of the elite who prioritize worldly gain over divine pleasure.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  narrates  that  the  Holy  Prophet (s.a.w.s.)  said,  “A  time  will  come  when  my  Ummah  will become impure from inside and attractive from outside in order  to  acquire  wealth.  They  will  do  showoff  instead  of gaining divine rewards. They will not fear Allah. Allah will punish all of them. At that time, people will supplicate like a drowning man but their supplications will not be accepted.”
